An interface with a call signature and nothing else describes a function. `type Handler = (event: Event) => void` says the same thing in one line.

Inline object types and `new (...)` signatures are checked too. An interface that extends another interface is left alone.

`--fix` rewrites the interface to a type alias, and the object type to a function type. Comments next to the signature move in front of the new type. A type alias can't be declared twice, so an interface whose name is declared again in the file is reported but not fixed. Other files add to an interface in a declaration file, a `namespace` or a `declare module` block, so only `--fix-dangerously` rewrites those.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"@typescript-eslint/prefer-function-type" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
interface Handler {
  (event: Event): void;
}

function listen(callback: { (event: Event): void }) {}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
type Handler = (event: Event) => void;

function listen(callback: (event: Event) => void) {}
```

A type with another member, or with more than one call signature, can't be written as a function type:

{/* good */}
```ts
interface Logger {
  (message: string): void;
  level: number;
}

interface Parse {
  (text: string): object;
  (text: string, strict: boolean): object;
}

interface Timed extends Logger {
  (message: string): void;
}
```

In an interface, `this` as a type means the interface itself. A function type has no such `this`, so the rule points at it and doesn't offer a fix:

{/* bad */}
```ts
interface Chain {
  (step: string): this;
}
```
